pages.title: Searching for the interpretation that changes the interpretation
pages.summary: A direct statement of purpose and a method for comparing canonical and noncanonical evidence without collapsing manuscript dates, canon history and empire.

pages.title: How the argument developed: Jesus, resurrection and empire
pages.summary: Trace the historical-Jesus hypothesis, Paul, later Gospel narratives, countertexts and the move to a first-century imperial question.

pages.title: Early creeds, angels and resurrection evidence
pages.summary: Examine 1 Corinthians 15, Philippians 2, Colossians 1, Hebrews 13 and angelic hospitality, separating early testimony from later interpretive claims.

pages.title: Imperial pressure and the Gospel Pilate
pages.summary: Compare Gospel portrayals of Pilate with Philo and Josephus, testing accommodation and anti-imperial readings without assuming state authorship.

pages.title: Competing crosses and the imperial-capture hypothesis
pages.summary: Connect the Pilate inquiry to contrasting crucifixion interpretations, testing partial and contested capture rather than a single coordinated rewrite.

pages.title: The laughing Jesus: crucifixion and authority in the Apocalypse of Peter
pages.summary: Read the living Jesus, suffering counterpart and critique of bishops and deacons in NHC VII,3, with precise manuscript locators and political implications.

pages.title: The Gospel of Truth: the cross as knowledge
pages.summary: Follow Error, the fruit of knowledge and the living book, preserving the text’s positive account of Jesus’s death and its uncertain attribution.

pages.title: Ransom, revelation and defeated rulers
pages.summary: Compare Mark’s service and ransom, Paul’s ignorant rulers, Colossians’ defeated powers and the overlapping Nag Hammadi accounts of salvation.

pages.title: Canon, coercion and the survival of Nag Hammadi
pages.summary: Distinguish early boundary-making, Constantine’s coercive measures, Athanasius’s list and competing explanations of the books’ preservation.

pages.title: Mandaean origins: John the Baptist, migration and rival memory
pages.summary: Investigate whether Mandaean ancestors knew John or fled after his execution, comparing western-migration arguments, Mesopotamian evidence and the limits of later sacred history.

pages.title: The Director’s Cut: Constantine, consolidation and Christian diversity
pages.summary: Trace diverse early Christian responses and the distinct stages of imperial patronage, councils, coercion, manuscript copying and canon formation.

pages.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls: Jewish diversity, Roman power and the limits of a straight line
pages.summary: Read textual plurality, Enochic traditions, light and darkness and the Roman Kittim as evidence for a varied Jewish world, while testing proposed later connections.

pages.title: Eusebius and Walter Bauer: who gets to call the beginning orthodox?
pages.summary: Compare apostolic continuity and heresy as deviation with Bauer’s 1934 regional challenge, its scholarly reception, and the limits of the surviving evidence.
